title: Find Words Formable from Characters
statement:
You are given a dictionary of `n` lowercase English words and a string `chars` of available lowercase letters. Each character of `chars` is a single tile that can be used **at most once**, so a letter that appears `c` times in `chars` can be used up to `c` times within one word. A dictionary word can be **formed** if it can be spelled using the tiles, in any arrangement (not every tile has to be used).

Find all dictionary words that can be formed from `chars`.

- The dictionary may contain the same word several times; report each distinct word only once.
- Print the words in increasing lexicographic (alphabetical) order.
- If no word can be formed, print `NONE`.

**Follow-up:** A common first approach is to build a trie of the dictionary and test every permutation of the characters. Think about why that does not scale, and how a count (anagram signature) comparison per word avoids it.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The next `n` whitespace-separated tokens are the dictionary words.
The last token is the string `chars`.
outputFormat: Print the formable distinct words in increasing lexicographic order on one line, separated by single spaces, or `NONE` if there are none.
constraints: All words and `chars` consist of lowercase English letters

tea
eat

examples.explanation: The tiles are `t`, `n`, `e`, `a` (one of each). `tea`, `eat`, `net` and `ten` fit. `tent` needs two `t`, `tee` needs two `e`, and `antenna` needs more tiles than are available.
The tiles are `o`, `k`, `b`, `o`. `book` needs two `o` and one each of `b` and `k`, so it fits; it appears twice in the dictionary but is printed once.
Neither word can be spelled from the tiles `a`, `b`, `c`.

complexity.time: O(total length of all words + |chars| + d log d)

hints: Whether a word can be formed does not depend on the order of its letters, only on how many times each letter occurs.
Count the letters of `chars` once. For each word, compare its letter counts against those: the word fits if no letter is needed more often than it is available.
Deduplicate the words (a set) and sort the survivors at the end; there is no need to generate permutations.
